contracts.summary: Reads the native name of one zero-based steel-design parameter block.
contracts.remarks: When to use: Use this name with the parameter-block overloads of GetMemberSteelUtilizationRatio and GetMemberSteelDesignResults. GetSteelDesignParameterBlockCount is a count, not a last index. This query passes the nonnegative index unchanged; it does not enumerate blocks, select a design code, run design or verify that all blocks are supported. Native false is failure; unwritten or empty successful names are rejected rather than used as a default block.

contracts.summary: Reads a member utilization ratio for one explicitly named steel-design parameter block.
contracts.remarks: When to use: Unlike the member-only overload, this calls the multiple-block native API and retains the exact requested ParameterBlockName in the result. The reviewed help describes AISC 360-16 multiple-design results; native availability and applicable code/context remain STAAD decisions. It does not select a block or take a maximum across blocks. Only finite nonnegative ratios are data; the single-block -999/-1 sentinels are not reused here. Native false takes precedence over any ratio buffer.

contracts.summary: Reads the native maximum utilization ratio for one member across available design parameter blocks.
contracts.remarks: When to use: Choose this to ask STAAD for its maximum across parameter blocks, rather than the member-only or explicitly named-block ratio query. The native output does not identify a governing block, so ParameterBlockName is null and no identity is guessed. A finite nonnegative ratio is required on native true; it is not converted to PASS/FAIL and no managed envelope, single-block sentinel interpretation or design execution occurs.

contracts.summary: Reads the named parameter-block steel-design packet for one analytical member.
contracts.remarks: When to use: Unlike GetMemberSteelDesignResults(memberId), this native packet supplies code, PASS/FAIL text, critical/allowable ratios, critical load case, clause and section for an explicit block. It supplies no critical station, FX/MY/MZ or slenderness; those fields are absent from ParameterBlockSteelDesignResults, never synthesized as zero. PASS/FAIL text is classified explicitly; other written text remains Unknown. Exact requested block and native status text are preserved. Native false prevents publication of any packet; no block selection, case activation or design is performed.

contracts.summary: Reads the native model-wide minimum steel-design failure ratio.
contracts.remarks: When to use: This function has no member ID or parameter-block input. It is a model-wide native failure-ratio observation, not the minimum utilization of a requested member or a managed envelope. GetMaximumSteelDesignFailureRatio is a separate observation with its own success flag; the two are not combined into an allegedly atomic range. Native false means failure or unavailable data without proving the absence of failing members. A finite nonnegative ratio is required on native success.

contracts.summary: Reads the native model-wide maximum steel-design failure ratio.
contracts.remarks: When to use: This function has no member ID or parameter-block input. It is independent from GetMinimumSteelDesignFailureRatio and from GetMaximumMemberSteelUtilizationRatio, which targets a member across blocks. No governing member/block is returned or invented. Native false prevents consumption of its output; the method does not infer failure thresholds, result freshness or an engineering PASS/FAIL decision.
